title: Takht Damdama Sahib
hookLine: at Talwandi Sabo, where the Granth was completed

lines: Well-known FOR AN HOUR, OR FOR A PAUSE.
THE ROAD COMES DOWN TO TALWANDI SABO.
cards: Some places are well-known for a single dramatic hour. Others are remembered for a pause. Follow the Tenth Guru's road, as this path has told it: Anandpur left behind, the sons lost, Chamkaur, Muktsar.
Then the road comes down into dry, flat country in the south of Punjab, to a village called Talwandi Sabo. And there, for a while, the chase ends.
Tradition says the Guru stayed, and that what happened next had nothing to do with swords.

teach.h: DAMDAMA: A PLACE TO CATCH BREATH.
teach.b: Damdama is the name the place carries, and tradition reads it as a place to catch your breath, to rest. What kind of rest? Not idleness.

Sikh tradition says that at Damdama Sahib the Guru completed the Granth: the scripture Guru Arjan had compiled was written out again, with the hymns of Guru Tegh Bahadur, the Tenth Guru's father, added in.
This path has told how Bhai Mani Singh sat as scribe. Today, look at the Guru's side of it. The rest after a long, hard road was spent on words, not weapons; on getting the book right.
Tradition holds that this is the version the Guru later named as Guru.

teach.h: A WORKING REST, AFTER THE STORM.
teach.b: So it was a working rest, the kind that comes after a storm, when someone finally has the stillness to set down what matters most.

teach.h: GURU KI KASHI: A CITY OF LEARNING.
teach.b: Tradition adds that the place became a center of learning, where scribes copied the Granth and students came to study, and Sikhs have called it Guru ki Kashi, the Guru's city of learning.
It's one of the five Takhts the Ardas remembers, and Sikhs connect it to this completing of the Granth.

Take the week together: penance as service, the Akal Takht's voice, the jathedar, the five, and three Takhts, one facing the Harmandir, one on the hill of beginnings, and this one, keeping the memory of a pause.
Authority, in this block, keeps turning out to be quiet: five people, a closed room, and a Guru resting long enough to finish a book.

how: Takht Damdama Sahib at Talwandi Sabo marks where Sikh tradition says Guru Gobind Singh stayed after years of war and the Granth was completed; Sikhs also call the place Guru ki Kashi.

games.q: you're the Tenth Guru, at last free of pursuit at Talwandi Sabo. how do you spend the rest?
o: raise a new army at once.
complete the Granth, word by word.
games.why: tradition says he spent it on the Granth, with Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns added: words, not weapons.

practice: Breathe out a little longer than you breathe in, and see flat, dry country, a village, a shade tree, and a tired traveler sitting down at last, with only quiet and then, slowly, the sound of words being read aloud and written down.
If the last stretch of your life has been a hard road, let this be a small Damdama, a place to catch your breath, and rest.
